reviews.text: 同样是玩过demo后，立刻就进行了购买。首先我主动清除了之前demo保留的进度，以便重新游玩时的体验，但是只用了1.5小时就基本打到了最后关卡，其中大部分关卡的怪物基本上是重复设计没有任何的特色，无非是数值的堆砌。其次需要瞄准或是摇奖的地方太快，是否射中和选中往往影响你这个回合的成效，对于想要休闲游玩的玩家体验不是很好。如果能忍受以上，该游戏的rouge玩法以及画风还算不错的。属于定价也不是特别贵的精致小品类游戏 没有快进后面的关卡比较浪费时间，道具解锁方式也很迷。 部分流派完全没有可玩性，希望后面会有更新

I think the game isn’t worth its price because it lacks depth. There’s only one viable build for the arena: the bow, the x2, and the hammer that gives % damage during the turn. I reached 26,551,448 damage in about 3 hours, but I stopped because it no longer made sense. I could never die due to the stun effect, and my damage scaling had become extremely slow, but I could have kept going for another 24 hours without ever dying.

内容太少，游戏框架也有大问题，作者打算让咱们目押这个老虎机，这样抓的所有牌就都能用了，从这个意义上游戏的构筑策略是有一定合理性的，但实操上老虎机这个作为核心玩法简直坐大牢，真不如搞成幸运房东那样的纯随机，我猜作者也发现了这么几个格子玩起来受限极大，又加入了主动道具这么个补充数值的东西，然后再限制金币上限鼓励你去用，这一切都是为了不断合理化老虎机这个核心机制做出的退让，然而这只会让整个游戏变得臃肿而不知所谓罢了 再补充一点：钻石和电锯的配合很破坏游戏平衡，而且对游戏机制很不健康，因为要发挥它的最大实力必须缩小卡组，也就没有任何策略性可言，但讽刺的是，这是唯一一个设计来规避老虎机机制的东西，然后它是最强的，这就很能说明问题了

Presentation is great, sound is great, the Idea is generally cool. It comes with a few major problems: 1.) The gambling through slot machine gameplay doesnt work well, because its not plannable or influential enough. You can try to line up by pressing stop at the right time, but it still ends up to be too much of a gamble to call it skill. Because of it not needing skill but being random/luck based, the entire gameplay consists of pressing a button and creating your "build" out of a too narrow selection of items/symbols. Picking new symbols is rarely a good idea, because why would you add another weapon lvl 1 decreasing your chance to hit your existing lvl 3 weapon? I asked that myself a lot while playing and came to the conclusion that the game has a design problem OR lacks complexity to provide valuable effects. Theres also no combos or dependencies, no chain effects or anything going on, supporting the use of symbol combinations. Some sort of combo sets that you can get would have added a lot of depth. Like hitting with 3 different types of daggers causes another roll or shield and hammer causes Shield Bash which adds the armor to your damage and stuns. 2.) The main problem through all of that, is the content is not there. In my less than 2 hours (112 minutes) i unlocked nearly all items (only 3 more to go) and got to the final level (failed it sadly). That means i am about 20 minutes short to finish the game in its entirety. I could run endless mode, but honestly, the gameplay isnt complex enough to entertain you for that. Theres not enough items and mechanics present in the game, that would warrant experimenting with different builds. Weapons arent that different, but overall the system has several issues that causes a lack of variation or "point". 3.) Games systems limit variety and reason. Theres a few different weapons, but frankly they arent really different. The weapons lack uniqueness to set them off of others and so it doesnt really matter what you pick. Ok that one weapon does lifesteal, that one causes poison, the other can stun the enemy, the other deals damage and magic damage. Sounds different on paper, but in reality isnt worth much of a thought when it comes to the gameplay. You will end up picking the poison dagger because not only does poison go through enemy armor, its also dealing far more reliable damage than any other weapon. "But lifesteal sounds so strong", but isnt. Because lifesteal doesnt do much when you are dead in one hit. This will only get worse even with more health and armor. Armor has a max amount of 100, so its pointless to stack more armor anyway. Even worse, the lifesteal isnt good enough anyway to keep you alive. All of this gets undermined by a meta progression ability, that automatically heals you after every round (HP regeneration), which is fast to level up and heals you significantly enough, that it overshadows any lifesteal you can do. Stun Hammer sounds good on paper, but the stun rarely happens and is an overall not interesting effect anyway. Even when critical striking, you stun the enemy for one action at max and i had fights that went for over 6 rounds with several times hitting the enemy but not stunning even once. The rest of the cast is just different damage numbers. The benefit between magic and physical damage feels insignificant to even make a that difference of adding two damage types. Like, i get it, magic ignores armor. But enemies rarely come with armor. In general poison outclasses any other effect and damage. I dont understand why magic spells like "fireball" exist, when you cant set enemies on fire. The passive perks have the same issue. You will find only: get lifesteal (as mentioned an irrelevant perk), increase damage, increase max life. The game doesnt provide interesting perks that change rules, like "lifesteal adds armor" or "hitting critical gives you another reroll". There occasionally are some minor effects like this, but very rarely, less significant and less interesting. The game is too less game, offers too less content and isnt designed well enough. Its minimalistic in every way and catches the hype of other recent slot machine/luck based games. Minimalistic however, isnt a good thing here. I recommend ignoring this title and instead of paying a bit less and get less, rather pay a bit more and pick something like Clover Pit and get a far better and more fleshed out game. Hate to say it, but thats what it is. Or get Dungeon Clawler, Ballionaire or Dicemancer, maybe Dicealot. This feels like a budget version. The only thing that is good here is the presentation. It has a great style. Yet it needed at least a full year of development to add more complexity and content. Im sorry, i dont feel it here.

I really wanted to like Slots & Daggers, but it feels too short and shallow. The slot machine roguelike concept is cool, but there is not enough variety to keep things interesting. Compared to Balatro, which builds tons of depth from a simple idea through strong synergies and run variety, Slots & Daggers feels solved very quickly. Once you get the few key items, most runs play out the same. Nearly every build relies on the same core items that give extra spins, so it becomes more about speeding through fights than making decisions. I finished my first run within my first few hours and unlocked almost everything shortly after. It is not a bad game, but it does not have enough content or replayability for me to recommend it.

五小时极速通关，总体来说可以给到八分，是一款以老虎机为基础设计的肉鸽游戏。 游戏的优缺点都非常明显： 优点——以老虎机转盘为核心设计了一个既看运气又看构筑的肉鸽游戏，且玩下来不会感觉到特别明显的缺点和问题，可谓“逻辑自洽”。 缺点——游戏内容不够丰富和整体流程过短 其中缺点展开说就是，游游戏内存在的构筑流派实在是很少，各种道具和随机性也不太足，导致真正强力的流派可能就那么一两种。 但只要你接受了这是一款小制作的游戏这个设定，那么这款游戏确实可以让玩家非常上头，我就是一口气摇了五个小时的转盘，现在还有点意犹未尽。

The designer lacks the basic understanding of what a fun game is. It works because it mimics some of the good similar games. but it falls short on every aspect, the build making, the rogue lite (which is always a downside but its done to achieve something, here its just a rogue lite maybe because its popular genre; (and no Balatro is a rogue-like not a rogue-lite) Play die in the dungeon, or Balatro, or if you want slot machine fun; play luck be a landlord. which is 100 times better. The main issue with this game is how grindy it is. you don't know if you are improving or not because how much you can get stronger by just buying upgrades and repeating the game. I am fine with unlockable but to give me an impossible game that I can keep clicking buttons and get so much stronger without even knowing what's a good strat or what is a good build is just plain bad. The executables (skill checks) add an unneeded layer of noise. it gives you a bit of fun because it lacks in build-making, and then you realize the skill checks weapons are just overall better weapons, another game design sin with understanding what is (high risk high rewards) and these weapons easily turn into dominant strats. To be completely fair; This is a fun game but everything its trying to mimic is more fun. so go play those other games.

It's a neat game, but there just isn't enough of it. I had the strategy figured out and beat the game in under 3 hours. The rest of the playtime was for the Arena mode, where I beat an enemy that was clearly intended to be impossible and then the game just threw me into the start of the main story rather than give any sort of ending. Balance is generally messed up. The obviously good options are so obviously good that there's little thought into how you maximise your strategy. And if you figure out the really busted build the game basically plays itself. It's a fun little puzzle to figure out for the first hour or two but there's not enough to justify the price tag.

[h1] Interesting game with very poor hardware optimisation [/h1] The game is way too demanding on the hardware for what it does. I have an old laptop running ubuntu and I'm able to play slay the spire 2 no problem. This game turns my laptop into a Panini grill. If you look solely at the game mechanics, you could run this in a browser or even with pen and paper and some dice. In it's current state, it's very poorly optimised. This is a pity as the idea is interesting and I was looking forward to exploring this nice casual game, but ended up requesting a refund.

TL:DR - I want to rate Slots & Daggers neutral. It really is a great game and worth the experience at the price tag. I would say full price is worth it, even more so at a discount. [b]As of this review, the last update to the game was Nov, 2025. Seems like the dev isn't returning as of right now. [/b] [b]The Good[/b] + Interesting idea implemented well + Challenging at times + Low price tag + Nice soundtrack + Overall fun + Replayable for different builds / fully unlocking items [b]The Okay[/b] ~ Balancing issues (once you figure out a build, it works too well) ~ Short, but sweet [b]The Bad[/b] - Balance issues kills the longevity [b]What I Would Want[/b] * Incentive to replay main game (i.e Escalation rank - difficulty increase + modifiers) * Of course more unique items, weapons, enemies, etc. * Balance fixes

Overall 7.5/10 A classic turn-based RPG with a twist, backed by great graphics and sound designs. Graphics 7.5/10 The graphics feels nostalgic, blending 90s inspired design with a clean modern look. Every action give a great feedback that makes it feels satisfying, especially the coin movement movement in particular is really well done. Loved it Sound 8.5/10 The sound design is the main star of this game. As the dev said in the trailer, it really captures that mechanical, physical slot machine feel, giving your brain a satisfying dopamine hit. Not only that but the timing and placement for the SFX is really well done IMO. Gameplay 6.5 The game loop is pretty short and easy to understand, making it easy for players to want to play one more run. Using slots as a mechanic to decide your action for the turn is a pretty neat idea. It creates that excitement of what will come out next, but that's also it's downside. The player doesn't feel in control. It feels more like a deck building game with auto-battle turned on. And that's why I think the player skill-check action is the most fun mechanics of this game. Because you can control it! However, because actions with skill checks are so strong, actions without them feel almost obsolete. That makes me feel like the game isn’t very well balanced. The progression is also very linear. The game blocks you with stat checks, so if you are not strong enough, you simply won’t be able to clear it. Enemies can OTK you if you don’t have enough power-ups, which makes it feel like you lost because of the game’s stat requirements, not because of your own decisions. What makes roguelikes fun is that even when you are underpowered, there is always a sense of "Hope" that you can turn things around. But this game doesn’t give the player that feeling; it never makes you believe that you can clear the game if you are underpowered. But overall, because of it's low price I think it's worth a try if you want to play something different!

Slots & Daggers is interesting in many ways, especially its art. However, once you start playing and spending some time with it, everything suddenly becomes boring. Although it has a structure similar to Clover Pit, it doesn't manage to be as layered and deep. The game ends in about 3-4 hours, and you constantly do the same things: the same power-ups, the same attacks, you keep repeating the same things over and over. The game also allows you to start from where you left off, but this is completely deceptive. You need to play from the first level to strengthen your hand; otherwise, you remain very weak. The gold strategy becomes ineffective after a certain point. There's no point where strategizing is rewarded. The gold you earn just starts accumulating because you've already acquired all the upgrades you can get in that session. While Slots & Daggers is interesting in terms of its art and core gameplay loop, its descent into boring repetition disappointed me. I congratulate the development team for their work. There's a real vision here, and I commend it, but the game needs to be more multi-layered. Hopefully, we'll have the chance to see more successful, longer, and better games from them in the future.

Slots & Daggers is a relatively enjoyable slot machine incremental-roguelike, with a focus on the rather charming design quality of the UI. Face of against enemies turn-based style by applying different abilities to your potential slot rolls, and use currency won through runs to increase your potential abilities and do it again! There isn't much more to be said about it beyond that, as it has been stuck in a near-release state for just about a year now. The developer mentioned they where taking 'a few days to step away from the project' before beginning to work on updates. However, there has been nothing but silence, leading me to assume the project is in a finalized state. I'd recommend waiting for any confirmation of content updates before picking it up, as there is an argument to be made about the price compared to content.

All right, so every other opinion is either written by bots or uses AI because they are so stupid. I'm going to be honest here so you can know if you want this game or not: it's a good game for dopamine, but there are four issues with it. And I'm going to talk only about issues. Firstly, it's genuinely so f^cking short. Maximum four hours if you have an average IQ. Mostly because even after end-game, you have nothing to do anyway since all of the items are unlocked. Secondly, half of the items are relatively useless, but once you have a good strategy - mine was inf coins with the gambling gem and money % amplifier - you can pretty much win the whole game, even with zero personal upgrades from the tokens. Thirdly, the game is unbalanced as hell, which is kind of bad for an rpg. So many items don't make sense because they're so bad[Which is pretty serious when the game has like, what, 30 items max?], and you'll pretty much be forced to do skill shots with physical weapons and amplifiers throughout the entire game. Essentially, every run is the same. Nothing differs at all. It goes like this: 1 - You pick a heavy sword, a coin and a shield as a starting kit, cuz everything else is trash, like I said before. 2 - You upgrade the heavy sword and make your own kit [like a large shield and a coin bag, for example]. 3 - You again just upgrade everything while buying and upgradeing random artefacts that you like. You will most likely get the Dracula artefact which has lifesteal, the cheese gouda that gives you more hp and the Undertale Heart of Determination that let's you re-roll if your crit, since everything is again, trash. Yeah, this is the thing in this game, once you notice the good items, everything else is indeed trash. 4 - You get the diamond, the saw and 2x items in the last lands, and you upgrade them fully since it's just free spins and everything else is trash. 5 - You defeat all the bosses and it's the end of the game since you pretty much one shoot nearly everyone if you're good. You don't buy more items, since they are simply trash. I for example one shooted final boss with a single turn, not knowing it was the final boss lmao It was so underwhelming. Fourthly, why does this game even have magical abilities? I understand that bosses have them [they bypass our shield and attack our HP directly which is scary... for the first four seconds], but it's useless FOR US when all the bosses have a maximum shield of 100-200, which is nothing, and the rest is pure health. What's the point of Shield bypassing weapons for me to use, if the bosses have zero shield in the first place? I think there is only one boss in the entire game that has a whole gimmick around having a massive amount of shield. One out of fifty. And he's still easy to beat, since he deals less damage than the first egg that we fight. Plus, the only magical items we get are a useless knife with lifesteal, a useless fireball and a coin-based magical gun that is objectively not worth it, even if you have inf coins. I have no idea why magic was added to this game for us. So, if you're willing to pay for a game that will last a maximum of four hours, then go for it. It's not bad; it's just an easy and fast way to get a dopamine hit. No wonder devs do not update it anymore, it genuinely has so many issues. 5.5/10 max. I can't believe I'm saying this, but even a game like Black Souls is more enjoyable than this. And that's saying something, since I ♥♥♥♥ on that game too.
